spec_match.rationale: Benchmarks the exact motivation chromestatus cites (single round-trip getAllRecords vs per-record cursor tasks) with a real store and real timings, and probes the exact prototype surface.

interactive.rationale: Record-count input, seed and two benchmark buttons with live gauges and a capped event log — all driven in this session with real results.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The lede promises reproducing the 350ms-class speedup locally; the page delivers a genuine measurable comparison (observed 304.3ms vs 233.8ms on 5000 rows here).

edge_cases.rationale: Unsupported branch shows a visible warn block and keeps the cursor benchmark usable, count is clamped 100..50000; but clicking any button in the ~100ms before the async db open completes is silently swallowed (db is undefined, the handler rejects, nothing is logged) — the init-race anti-regression case.

references.rationale: Links https://chromestatus.com/feature/5124331450138624 and the spec's getAllRecords anchor.

conformance.rationale: Feature-level suite probes the real surface; untouched (immutable).

runtime_evidence.rationale: Cloud-fallback verification, NOT chrome-devtools-mcp (auto-research.md §0 blocker applies): headless Chromium 141 + raw CDP — support banner hidden (API present), seeded 5000 rows, cursor 304.3ms vs getAllRecords 233.8ms, speedup gauge 1.30×, log ordered correctly; immediate-click race reproduced (empty log, no feedback); screenshot read. Not exercised: the unsupported branch (needs a pre-133 browser).

telemetry_health.rationale: No showcaseTelemetry.assert for the benchmark contract; the swallowed early-click rejection would surface as an unhandled-rejection telemetry event rather than an intentional assert.

design_system.rationale: All colours via design-system variables; gauges use --bg-stone/--text-black, win gauge --accent-emerald on stone (AA for large numerals); warn block uses --accent-rose border with charcoal text.

accessibility.rationale: Native labelled controls and keyboard operability, but the gauges and event log are not live regions, so benchmark results are visual-only for screen readers; the log prepends entries, which is also hostile to virtual-cursor reading order.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: auto-fit minmax(180px,1fr) gauges and wrapping controls read clean at desktop; the ≈360px touch class was not exercised in this session and the demo's responsive-support record predates this review.

openQuestions.title: Guard the pre-init click window
openQuestions.detail: db is assigned by an async IIFE; a click on seed/run in the first ~100ms finds db undefined and the async handler rejects silently — no log line, no state change (reproduced via CDP: immediate seed click left the log empty). Add a one-line guard in each handler (if (!db) { log('db still opening — try again'); return; }) or disable the buttons until the open completes.

openQuestions.title: Announce benchmark results to screen readers
openQuestions.detail: Give the gauges row (or the log) role=status / aria-live=polite so 'cursor: 5000 rows in 304ms' is announced; consider appending log entries instead of prepending so reading order matches chronology.

openQuestions.title: Compare against getAll+getAllKeys as a third bar
openQuestions.detail: The feature's second half (direction option for getAll/getAllKeys) is absent here; a third benchmark running the legacy two-request pattern would complete the comparison the feature index promises and quantify what the single-call shape saves beyond cursors.

summary: Weekly hardening critique 2026-10-18 (headless Chromium 141 + raw CDP cloud fallback, not chrome-devtools-mcp; URL /v133/indexeddb-getallrecords-and-direction-option-for-getall-getallkeys/cursor-vs-getallrecords/): a genuinely working, honest benchmark — real 5000-row store, cursor 304.3ms vs getAllRecords 233.8ms (1.30×), correct support probe on the exact prototype member, clean console in normal flow. Gaps: a reproduced init race silently swallows clicks before the async db open resolves, results are visual-only for screen readers, and the direction-option half of the feature has no bench bar.
